what_happened: The job "Publish the first firstmate explainer page to GitHub Pages" failed at admission. The change touched .github/workflows/pages.yml, a governance file. Such a file can only be changed when the accepted reading lists it as a deliverable and names it in an acceptance criterion. The reading did not do that, so admission refused the change and the job ended failed with no page published.
cause: Reading of the request happens without knowing which files the outcome will require changing. "Publish to GitHub Pages" implies a deploy workflow, but nothing at intake maps outcomes to governance files. The protection rule is only enforced at admission, after the reading is accepted, so the mismatch shows up as a failed job rather than a corrected reading.
prevention: At reading time, run a check that predicts the files a job will change, for example from the repo's Pages configuration and existing workflows. If any are governance files, require the reading to list them as deliverables and name them in an acceptance criterion before it is accepted. Otherwise send the reading back for revision. This catches the whole class before admission, not after a failed job.
proposed_request: Publish the first firstmate explainer page so it is live on GitHub Pages and reachable at its public URL. The deliverables include the explainer page content and the Pages deployment workflow .github/workflows/pages.yml, which may be created or changed. Acceptance criteria: (1) .github/workflows/pages.yml deploys the page to GitHub Pages on merge to the default branch; (2) the explainer page is present in the published site; (3) the public Pages URL returns the page with HTTP 200.
